newsitem.title: UK: Bank of Scotland lifts pre-tax profit.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Scotland lifts pre-tax profit.

text.p: Bank of Scotland on Wednesday posted a 22 percent rise in pre-tax profits for the year to the end of February, above the top end of analysts' expectations.

Pre-tax profits rose to 664.1 million pounds ($1.1 billion) compared to 545 million pounds in the previous year while total dividend jumped 20 percent to 8.22p per share from 6.85p per share last time.
Bank of Scotland Governor Sir Bruce Pattullo said the rise in profits was based on the "ongoing development of the scope and professionalism of its businesses".
Taking out exceptional gains in the previous year's figures, Bank of Scotland said its pre-tax profit rise would have been an even healthier 27 percent.
This year's figures included a full contribution for the first time from its Australian unit BankWest which made a profit of 71.6 million pounds ($116.9 million).

The Bank said its cost to income ratio had fallen comparing the second half of the year with the first despite a hefty rise in operating expenses. This is partly explained by the inclusion of a full year of BankWest as opposed to three months in last year's accounts. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
